title: High-Protein Turkey Chili
shortDescription: Big pot, lean protein, hall fuel
subtitle: Big pot, lean protein, hall fuel
description: Big pot, lean protein, hall fuel. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for High-Protein Turkey Chili in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Kidney beans, drained as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch turkey. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the pots
steps.instruction: Dice onions and peppers into even ¼-inch pieces. Mince garlic. Drain beans. Open tomatoes. Set out your largest stock pot (or two medium pots if feeding 10+). Line a sheet pan if you're making garlic bread on the side.

steps.title: Brown the meat
steps.instruction: Heat 2 tbsp oil in the pot over medium-high until it shimmers. Add ground turkey in two batches — don't crowd. Break into crumbles and cook until deeply browned with no pink (160°F+). You want fond on the bottom, not gray steam. Drain excess grease if the pot looks oily.

steps.title: Bloom spices
steps.instruction: Add onions and peppers; cook 6–8 minutes until edges soften and smell sweet. Stir in garlic, chili powder, smoked paprika, and cumin for 45 seconds until fragrant. Add tomato paste and brown sugar; cook 1 minute until the paste darkens slightly.

steps.title: Simmer the chili
steps.instruction: Pour in crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, broth, and beans. Bring to a gentle bubble, then lower to a steady simmer — small bubbles, not a rolling boil. Cook uncovered 35–40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes. High-Protein Turkey Chili is ready when it coats the back of a spoon and a drag through the pot leaves a clear trail. Season with salt and Worcestershire. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion High-Protein Turkey Chili onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Hold and serve the hall
steps.instruction: Keep on low (or transfer to a cambro) for late eaters. Set a topping bar: shredded cheese, diced onion, jalapeños, sour cream. Call the crew while it's hot — chili holds well but the first bowl is always the best.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Portion bowls on the line with protein visible on top — crew eats with their eyes first.
Keep dressing and crunchy toppings in side bowls so greens stay crisp through second servings.
Line up High-Protein Turkey Chili on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Big pot, lean protein, hall fuel. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — High-Protein Turkey Chili runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
